  You are revising ADR-0019 at D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md (project D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d, Godot 4.7.2 GDScript) after per-ADR engine and TD-ADR reviews and a cross-ADR adjudication of the Core tier.   ADR-0019 review verdict CONCERNS (1 blocking: E1). Idiomatic overall for 4.7.2: `_input` latch plus `_process` poll, runtime `InputMap` registration, `physical_keycode`, event-type device classification, `@abstract` ports, typed collections and caller-owned buffers all hold up. Re-probed headless on 4.7.2 and CONFIRMED probes 1, 2, 3 (-1 wildcard matches pad 2 and keyboard 5; a pad-0 binding does not match pad 2), 6 (same-frame press+release leaves just_pressed and just_released true and pressed false) and 10 (deadzone stored). Also confirmed that `_input` runs before the frame's `_process` with press/release order preserved (supports ADR-0001 § 3 item 3b). Probes 4, 5, 8, 9, 11 and 12 were not re-run but are plausible. Probe 10 only shows the 0.0 is stored, not what it does, and that behaviour is the E1 bug. Every window, warp, focus, wheel, SDL3 and release-export claim is correctly marked UNVERIFIED and gated on PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1.:
  E1 [high, BLOCKING] § 3.3 registers every action with `InputMap.add_action(name, 0.0)` and says this makes `MOVE_DEADZONE` and `AIM_DEADZONE` the only deadzones. Probed on 4.7.2: with a 0.0 deadzone an `InputEventJoypadMotion` with axis_value 0.0 reports `is_action_pressed` TRUE for both the positive and the negative direction action, because the engine's same-direction test accepts a zero value and `abs(0.0) >= 0.0`. A tiny 0.02 value is also 'pressed'. A trigger axis at rest (value 0.0) reports its action pressed. `Input.is_action_pressed` goes true for both `mv_r` and `mv_l` after one centred-stick event, while `get_action_raw_strength` correctly stays 0.0. Effects: `is_action_down` / `Input.is_action_pressed` is wrong for any action with a pad axis or trigger binding (move, aim, NAV, a trigger-bound run or interact); the `_input` edge latch records press edges for centred sticks and never sees a release, which breaks latch-until-released (§ 4.3), the hold-mode cancel, the resync comparison of the real `interact` state, and fills the EdgeRing. Probe 10 verified only that 0.0 is stored. The deadzone is not needed to keep raw strength raw: `get_action_raw_strength` ignores it.
    amendment: Replace 'zero engine deadzone' with a non-zero deadzone for every catalogue action (engine default 0.5, or the existing 0.2) and keep `MOVE_DEADZONE` / `AIM_DEADZONE` as Adapter-level scalings over `get_action_raw_strength`. Amend § 3.3, Alternative 6 and probe 10 ('stores 0.0') accordingly. Add a BindingFactory test: a centred JoypadMotion (0.0) and a trigger at rest do not make any action pressed, and `InputMap.action_get_deadzone` is never 0.0. Add a headless probe 13 with the p1 script: centred-stick event and trigger-at-rest, asserting both are not pressed.
  E2 [medium] § 3.1 and § 3.2 treat the Adapter as the single `_input` latch, and § 3.2 / R4 / OQ-B have it call `set_input_as_handled()` in `chart_table`. Probed: `_input` is delivered in REVERSE TREE ORDER (a later sibling first) and `process_priority` has no effect on `_input` order. Two nodes were tested, with the priorities swapped between runs, and the later sibling always received the event first and, when it handled it, the earlier sibling never saw it. `process_priority` -100 therefore orders only the Adapter's `_process`. Any node later in the tree that handles an event first (the Chart Table layer, HUD, the ADR-0031 debug overlay and `DevInputSink`) silently starves the Adapter's ring, which is a missed press with no error. `set_input_as_handled()` does not change `Input.*` poll state (actions update before dispatch), so only the ring is affected.
    amendment: State in § 3.1 that the composition root adds `InputAdapter` as the LAST child of the root so its `_input` runs first, and add a boot assertion plus a two-node unit test (copy of the probe). State that only the Adapter may call `set_input_as_handled()` for action-bound events, and that the dev overlay latches through the Adapter's `DevInputSink` rather than its own `_input`. Record in ADR-0001 § 3 item 3b that `_input` ordering is tree order, not priority.
  E3 [low] § 3.2, R4 and OQ-B write `set_input_as_handled()` as if it were a Node method. Probed: a Node script calling `set_input_as_handled()` is a parse error ('Function not found in base self'); the method is `Viewport.set_input_as_handled()`. `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` compiles and works from `_input`. The § 8.1 READ-01 symbol list also omits this token and the other device-adjacent engine members used in `EngineInputSource` (`get_mouse_position`, `warp_mouse`, `joy_connection_changed`, `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT`, `NOTIFICATION_WM_WINDOW_FOCUS_OUT`).
    amendment: Write `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` everywhere. Add `set_input_as_handled` to the § 8.1 symbol list (allowed only in `input_adapter.gd`), and decide whether the focus notifications and `joy_connection_changed` belong to the allow-listed files only.
  E4 [medium] § 3.2 records 'a press or release of a registered action (resolved with `InputMap.event_is_action`)' for every device event. For `InputEventJoypadMotion`, `is_action_pressed` is true on EVERY motion event while the stick is past the deadzone (probed: successive 0.7 and 0.9 events both report pressed). The ring would receive a duplicate 'press' per motion event per axis per frame, never a release record, which is an overflow and ordering hazard (`PC_EDGE_OVERFLOW` fail-safe becomes the normal path while a stick is held).
    amendment: Have `RawEvent.classify` treat `InputEventJoypadMotion` as continuous-only: no edge records. Derive stick and trigger edges (NAV, MOVE_DEADZONE crossings, trigger-bound actions) in the Adapter from `get_action_raw_strength` with the existing hysteresis, once per frame. Keep edge records for key, mouse button and joypad button events only, and de-duplicate against an Adapter held-set.
  E5 [medium] § 4.4 and § 6.3 depend on `MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED_HIDDEN`, `Input.set_mouse_mode` applied only on change, and `warp_mouse`. Not covered by the spike matrix and UNVERIFIED: (1) the docs restrict `warp_mouse` to Windows, macOS and Linux, and Wayland is a doubtful case; the budgets target RM-DECK, which is Linux. The spike lists only an editor session and a release export, not the Deck or gamescope. (2) The editor's embedded game window (4.4+) may not honour confine or warp, so a spike run in the embedded window would give false results. (3) If the OS drops confinement on focus loss or alt-tab, 'apply only on change' never re-applies it. `Input.warp_mouse` takes window coordinates and `Viewport.warp_mouse` takes viewport coordinates; they are equal only because the root has no stretch.
    amendment: Add to PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1: run (a), (b) and (e) on RM-DECK (Linux) and in a non-embedded window. Make `EngineInputSource` re-assert the cursor mode on every FOCUS_IN and PAUSED->RUNNING, not only on change. Specify the fallback when `warp_cursor` is a no-op: keep the stored `cursor_off` as a virtual cursor (accumulated `InputEventMouseMotion.relative`) so zoom and handover do not depend on warp. Name `Input.warp_mouse` (window pixels) as the one call used.
  E6 [low] § 3.7 says the Adapter keeps its own held ledger because `Input.release_pressed_events` is not exposed to GDScript (probe 9, plausible). The engine is believed to call it internally on main-window focus-out (UNVERIFIED), which would deliver synthetic release events through `_input` after the Adapter has already zeroed intents. `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT` is app-level (alt-tab to another app); a window drag or an OS modal dialog may only fire `NOTIFICATION_WM_WINDOW_FOCUS_OUT` or `Window.focus_exited`. That is already spike (e).
    amendment: Make release records for controls absent from the held ledger idempotent in the ring (no error, no counter), and have the focus handler connect all three signals and notifications to one latch. Record in spike (e) whether synthetic releases arrive via `_input`.
  E7 [low] § 3.2 and § 6.4 latch 'a mouse wheel notch with its sign'. A wheel is an `InputEventMouseButton` (WHEEL_UP / WHEEL_DOWN) delivered as a press immediately followed by a release; wheel events are not coalesced by `use_accumulated_input`; the wheel has a fractional `factor` on high-resolution wheels and precision touchpads, and horizontal wheel buttons also exist. A latch that counts both the press and the release, or ignores `factor`, double counts. Touchpad gestures arrive as `InputEventPanGesture` / `InputEventMagnifyGesture`, which classify as OTHER and are ignored (acceptable, but the user-visible effect on touchpads should be stated).
    amendment: Count only `pressed == true` wheel events, sum signs, ignore the paired release, ignore `factor` for the sign (one step per frame is already capped by § 6.4), and state that gesture events are ignored. Record the burst size in spike (c).
  E8 [low] § 3.3 builds every binding with `device = -1`, and user rebinds go through BindingFactory. Probed: a fresh `InputEventKey` carries device 16 and a mouse button 32, and real captured events carry the real device (or pad index). If the Settings rebind capture stores the captured event directly, the new binding is device-specific, which is the probe-3 trap again.
    amendment: Specify that the rebind capture path duplicates the captured event, sets `device = BINDING_ANY_DEVICE` and clears `pressed` / `echo` before `action_add_event`. Extend the § 8.3 factory test to cover user-capture events as well as the defaults.
  E9 [low] 4.7 typed-return rule and ports. `@abstract` on its own line before `class_name` / `extends`, with `@abstract func ... -> T` bodies, compiles on 4.7.2 (probed). A subclass that implements only some abstract methods is a parse error (probed), so `FakeInputSource` and `EngineInputSource` must implement all ten. Under the 4.7 override rule an override that omits its return annotation inherits the typed return and must return on every path, so a stub like `func cursor_px(): pass` fails. The fallback 'plain base class with `push_error` stubs' must also return a value. Typed `static func fields() -> Array[Dictionary]` over a `const ROWS: Array[Dictionary]` literal compiled and ran (probed); const arrays and dictionaries are read-only, which suits the schema list.
    amendment: Add to Implementation Guidelines: ports are `@abstract`, every override restates its return type and returns on every path (add `return 0` / `return Vector2i.ZERO` stubs in the Fake), and the lint pack flags an override without a return annotation. No Object-method name clash was found: the `get_*` accessors on `ControllerView`, `AdapterViews` and `MenuInputQueue`, `count()`, `clear()`, `setup()` and `on_result()` do not shadow Object or Node members.
  E10 [info] Plausibility notes. (a) § 3.3 calls `BINDING_ANY_DEVICE == InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_EMULATION` 'a coincidence'. Probed behaviour is that -1 is the engine's any-device binding wildcard (pad-0 binding misses pad 2; -1 matches pads 0 and 2 and keyboards 16 and 5), and 4.7.2 reports DEVICE_ID_EMULATION -1, KEYBOARD 16, MOUSE 32. The code does not depend on the equality, so this is harmless. (b) § 6.1 `floor(pos_curr)` on a `Vector2i` is legal and returns a `Vector2i` (probed) but is a no-op, and ADR-0015 exposes Body position as scalar getters (`pos_x`, `pos_y`), not a `Vector2i`. (c) Probe 12 (root `content_scale_mode` 0 in a bare script) says nothing about the project; ADR-0008 owns the stretch setting, and the 4.7 stretch default change applies to new-project templates only. (d) Packed-array columns (`snapshot`, `MenuInputQueue`) are safe: PackedArrays are reference types, § 2.7 duplicates them, and the 4.7 element-write-skips-setter change is irrelevant because the design forbids property setters (ADR-0004).
    amendment: Reword (a) to 'the engine's any-device wildcard; the code depends only on the constant'. Drop `floor()` in § 6.1 or restate it against ADR-0015's getter shape.
  
  ADR-0019 review verdict CONCERNS. The problem statement and rationale are clear. The nine alternatives were genuinely weighed, and the trade-offs in Consequences are honest. The engine is stamped as Godot 4.7.2, and the post-cutoff risks (4.7 device ids, 4.6 focus split, 4.5 SDL3 and @abstract) are flagged and probed. TR traceability is complete: all 49 TR ids tagged ADR-0019 in requirements-traceability.md appear in the ADR, and the stated 35/7/20 = 62 row split checks out. The technical-director ratifies PC-14 (Body owns position; the Controller owns intent, gait, aim, facing, state, carry and channel; the Controller holds no write on Body), subject to the amendments below. That ratification unblocks ADR-0015's dependency on it. Five items block Accept: (1) the chest point is derived one tick stale relative to the foot; (2) §7.2 contradicts ADR-0018 on where the beam Light2D sits; (3) the spike gate is stated three incompatible ways and the spike is not registered in architecture.md; (4) Key Interfaces disagree with §2.6 and the sibling ADRs; (5) two lints (CTL-08, CTL-04) forbid code the ADR itself decides on. The other findings are non-blocking but must be stated before Accept.:
  T1 [HIGH, BLOCKING] chest_sim and hand_sim are derived one tick stale. §2.4 step 7 computes them inside controller.step, which runs BEFORE body.integrate (§2.4; ADR-0015 hook order), so they use the previous tick's pos_curr. ADR-0017 D5.3 then reads chest_point as the beam apex and BodyView pos_curr as the occlusion origin, both in emitter.place, which runs after body.integrate. On every moving tick the apex therefore trails the foot origin by up to V_RUN px. That breaks the apex/occlusion consistency ADR-0018 is built on, and it makes the post_restore value (computed from the restored, post-integrate pos_curr) mean something different from the value seen in play. Three further gaps: the ADR never states that chest_point is an absolute body-frame point; it never says where the Controller Sim gets CHEST_POINT[sheet][anim] (§7.3 places that table in a presentation sidecar under assets/data/animation/); and ADR-0017 asked for 'two scalars', while Key Interfaces returns Vector2i.
    amendment: In §2.4 and §2.7, choose one of two options. (a) Store only the offset CHEST_POINT[sheet][anim row] mirrored by facing in step 7, and have the getters chest_x/chest_y(player_id) return BodyView.pos_x/pos_y(actor) plus the stored offset at read time, so the point is never stale. (b) Move the derivation to controller.noise, which is already after body.integrate with tolerates_stale false. State that the point is an absolute integer in the body frame. State that the sim reads CHEST_POINT and HAND_POINT per (sheet, anim row), with the anim row taken from loco_state, from a frozen ADR-0007 table injected via ControllerTuning or a ControllerCatalog. §7.3's bounds checks run on that same table. Publish the point as two int getters, or say explicitly that a Vector2i return value does not allocate. Add a unit test: on a moving tick, the apex used by emitter.place minus the CHEST offset equals the pos_curr of the same tick.
  T2 [HIGH, BLOCKING] §7.1 and §7.2 have the Avatar Presenter write 'the chest Light2D's position and rotation' through Placement.put, placing the light at the chest point. ADR-0018 (which owns the shadow-origin decision, mode B) requires the beam Light2D node to sit at the FOOT cell from body.state plus Placement.CELL_CENTRE, written through Placement.put_light_origin, with the chest point serving only as the cone apex. As written, the allow-list and the lint CTL-11 would accept the position ADR-0018 forbids, and would flag put_light_origin as an off-list write.
    amendment: Rewrite the §7.2 allow-list entry as follows: 'the beam Light2D's position through Placement.put_light_origin, at the interpolated foot cell plus CELL_CENTRE under ADR-0018 mode B (or whatever origin ADR-0018 selects), and its rotation (which may be fractional)'. In §7.1, add that the chest offset is read from ControllerView for the apex/offset terms only. Extend CTL-11's allow-list to put_light_origin. Add a cross-reference to ADR-0018 in Depends On or Related.
  T3 [HIGH, BLOCKING] The spike gating is stated three incompatible ways and is broader than the MVP needs. Engine Compatibility says PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 'gates acceptance of §§ 3.2, 4.4 and 6, not the block, commands or hooks'. The Ordering Note and Validation Criteria say acceptance of the WHOLE ADR requires spike items (a)-(c), (e) and (g); (e) and (g) gate §3.7 and §3.3, which are not in the first list. 'Blocks' then holds every Interaction, Assembly and Chart Table story that calls the Controller mutators or views until Accept. The net effect is that the sim half (block, commands, hooks, mutators, view), which needs no device hardware, waits on a spike that needs an XInput pad, a non-XInput pad, a letterboxed window at two zoom steps, and 125%/150% display scaling. That is heavy to require for a solo MVP. PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 is also missing from architecture.md § Spikes and from the spike order, and the Migration Plan does not add it (compare ADR-0005's explicit 'Spike-list sync').
    amendment: Replace the three statements with one gate table. Sim half (§1, §2, §7 except the Light2D origin, §8.2-§8.4 and the sim rows of §8.3) is accepted on Foundation ADR acceptance plus KRN-LAT-02. Adapter half (§3.2, the §3.3 wildcard, §3.7 focus, §4.4, §6): each spike item is marked either REQUIRED for acceptance (recommended: (a), (b), (h) on keyboard, mouse and one pad) or RECORDED (non-XInput pad, (c), (d), (e), (f), (g), (i)), and every RECORDED item names the fallback that ships if it fails (R3's per-device rebind; the stored cursor_off). Add PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 to architecture.md § Spikes and to the spike order after KRN-LAT-02, with the user's approval, as a Migration Plan line.
  T4 [MEDIUM, BLOCKING] Key Interfaces are not concrete or consistent enough for stories. (1) ControllerView omits getters that §2.2 marks as Published and that §2.6, §7.1 and TR-pc-017 list: run, aim_live, carry_ref, salvage_carry, channel_face, intent_run, stagger_end_tick and t_downed. It also lacks has_row(player_id), which ADR-0015 consumes for BDY_SEAT_UNBOUND (the ADR offers only row_count). (2) §2.6 says 'Body reads octant, gait_effective and intent_octant', but ADR-0015 (§ 'What Body reads', TR-shipbody-016) refuses intent_octant. (3) §1.1 lists a 'pod-body test' among body.state's published reads, but ADR-0015 says that test is not Body's, and this ADR's own assumptions put pod semantics on ADR-0026. (4) AdapterViews omits device_seq, focus_ref, self_target, aim_source and preplay_entry(i, out), all of which §3.9 names and ADR-0020 (focus echo) and ADR-0029 (pre-play tokens) consume. (5) MenuInputQueue has no producer-side signature and no field-index constants for get_field.
    amendment: List every published getter in Key Interfaces with get_<noun>(player_id) signatures, including get_has_row(player_id) -> bool (keep row_count for the give_up solo test). Strike intent_octant from the §2.6 sentence about Body's reads; Interaction and Assembly stay its readers. In §1.1 and §2.4, read IN_POD from a pod-body predicate owned by ADR-0026 (Web Map/Transit), which this ADR names as an assumption. Complete the AdapterViews signatures listed in §3.9 and add MenuInputQueue's push_* and the FIELD_A/B/X/Y constants.
  T5 [MEDIUM, BLOCKING] Two lints contradict the decision as written. CTL-08 bans the token 'attention.' in src/sim/controller/, but §2.4 requires controller.noise to call Attention's injected push_stimulus mutator once per moved tick, and any receiver named for Attention (for example _attention.push_stimulus) matches the banned token. CTL-04 bans writing 'any symbol naming a ControllerRow field' outside src/sim/controller/. Field names such as last_octant, facing and octant also exist in body.state (Body's last_octant, ADR-0015) and horror.state (ADR-0023 keeps last_octant), so a lexical rule will false-positive on legitimate owner code.
    amendment: Restate CTL-08 as a ban on Attention, Sanity and PERCEPTION_OUT reads: get_view(&"attention.state"), the AttentionView/SanityView types, perceived(, PerceptionRef and true_value. State the one allowed write: the injected Attention mutator object's push_stimulus, used only in controller_noise.gd. Restate CTL-04 as an AST rule over assignments whose receiver has static type ControllerRow, or over member access through the controller.state block object, outside src/sim/controller/. Each rule gets a good fixture covering the allowed case.
  T6 [MEDIUM] The determinism claims rest on a hash that cannot see the claimed outputs. §8.5 asserts that controller.state hashes match across 30/60/120/144 fps. ADR-0005 §4.3 takes block_hash over the snapshot payload, and §2.7 writes octant, intent_octant/run, gait_effective, ramp_ticks, walk_ticks, decel_k, stagger_end_tick and the channel fields as rest values, with the transient loco_states written as IDLE. The hash is therefore blind to most of the per-tick Controller output that TR-pc-039 is about; divergence surfaces only later, through body.state. The same normalisation means an ADR-0005 G4 run that snapshots while an intent is held diverges by construction: the restored run stops until a resync while the control run keeps moving.
    amendment: In §8.5, also compare per-tick samples of every ControllerView getter (or a test-only canonical encode of the live rows) across the four cadences. Add a Validation line: G4 and KRN-RST fixtures that include controller.state snapshot from rest intent, or replay the Adapter's resync submission. Record this as a cross-ADR note to ADR-0005.
  T7 [MEDIUM] Row lifecycle is undefined. §2.2 says player_id is written by 'default_state, seat creation', but neither default_state's contents nor the caller and scope that create a seat row are stated. ADR-0015 tolerates a missing row by treating it as v_eff 0 and counting BDY_SEAT_UNBOUND, so a missing creation path fails silently as a frozen avatar instead of a fault.
    amendment: State that default_state() returns the MVP payload with one row for the host PlayerId at rest values (or that init_world creates it in the INIT scope, with the caller named). State that a seat bound in body.state with no controller.state row after post_restore is a restore fault (PC_ROW_MISSING), or explicitly hand that check to ADR-0016's verifier list.
  T8 [LOW] The Migration Plan cites 'Foundation asks (below)', but no such section exists. Without exact text the asks will not be actioned: the cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter exception for AvatarFrames (registry entry owned by ADR-0001/ADR-0009); AdapterViews as an INPUT_ADAPTER-phase product readable by the AVATAR stage (ADR-0009's rule 'never read a product of the same or a later stage' does not cover a pre-driver phase); the ADR-0008 f_q read accessor; ADR-0010 rule-inventory rows for CTL-01..12; and the tr-registry.yaml wording changes for TR-pc-035 and TR-pc-018 (Class B to Class A).
    amendment: Add a '### Foundation asks' subsection listing each ask with its target ADR, its section, and the exact sentence to add or replace, plus the registry entry to update (cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter gains an exception clause scoped to AvatarFrames and referenced_by ADR-0019).
  T9 [LOW] Two small gaps and inconsistencies. (1) The Architecture Diagram says 'Input.* / InputMap / InputEvent (4 files only, § 8.1)', while §1.4, §8.1 and Consequences say five files. (2) §7 does not say how the Avatar Presenter's node is parented across bodies, although ADR-0034 assumes BodyScenes.attach_presenter(actor_id, node) at spawn and that the Presenter never reparents itself (the PROJECTOR does so on BODY_TRANSFER in stage 0).
    amendment: Change the diagram to '5 files'. In §7.1, add: 'The Presenter attaches its node with BodyScenes.attach_presenter(actor_id, node) at spawn, never reparents itself, and writes position in stage AVATAR after the PROJECTOR's stage-0 reparent (ADR-0034).'
  T10 [LOW] Right-sizing for a solo MVP. The context machine includes CHAT and the co-op overlay branches (§3.7, §4.2: 'in co-op the same press opens the overlay with the kernel RUNNING'), both of which are VS-B. The lint pack (11 rules with fixtures), four committed input tables and the four-cadence trace harness fit the project's ADR-0010 posture, but the MVP-versus-later boundary is not marked, so stories may build VS-B paths.
    amendment: Mark CHAT and the co-op branches 'VS-B: enum value and matrix column reserved, transitions not implemented at MVP; the matrix completeness check skips reserved columns'. In §8.2 and §8.3, tag which rules and tests are MVP-required.
  
  CROSS-ADR RULINGS (binding):
  CT-20 owner ADR-0015 (align: ADR-0014, ADR-0012, ADR-0013, ADR-0017, ADR-0019, ADR-0003): Merges the 0015-review budget item, plus a conflict the reviewers missed: the Core hook budgets on the worst-aligned tick (a Graph hook tick) sum to Graph 0.5 + Body 0.4 + Emitter 0.4 (EXPOSURE_BUDGET_MS, raisable to 0.6) + controller.step 0.16 (8 x 0.02) + layout.doors 0.2 = 1.66 ms against the 2.0 ms P3 target. If ADR-0014's 0.6 ms solid_in aggregate is counted on top of Body, the Core sum is about 1.86 ms, or 2.06 ms with the Emitter raised. That leaves 0.34 ms or less for the Suit, Interaction, Assembly, Web, Attention, Horror and Sanity hooks, and no document holds the ledger. Ruling: the hook owner's whole-hook figure is the ledger entry. ADR-0015's 0.05 ms per actor (0.4 ms for eight) wins, and ADR-0014's query share must fit inside it. No new numbers are invented here. The ledger itself is a foundation amendment to ADR-0003 (P3 semantics owner).
    amendment: ADR-0015 section 13: 'The ledger entry is the whole `body.integrate` hook: 0.05 ms per actor P99, 0.4 ms for eight, pending S1. It includes ADR-0014 `solid_in` calls, the clamp, the row copy and the dirty marks. S1 reports the whole-hook figure, with `solid_in` time as a sub-counter.' ADR-0014 section 11 and line 48 replace 'solid_in P99 at most 0.05 ms per actor, 8 actors at most 0.6 ms aggregate' with 'solid_in is a share of ADR-0015's whole-hook 0.05 ms per actor (0.4 ms for eight); S1 reports it as a sub-counter of body.integrate'. The Emitter-box line (0.3 ms) is charged inside ADR-0017's EXPOSURE_BUDGET_MS. # Global instructions (all projects)

## Dynamic Workflows: model choice

- Always use Sonnet 5.5 (`model: 'sonnet'`) or Haiku (`model: 'haiku'`) for worker agents in Dynamic Workflows (the Workflow tool's `agent()` calls), to preserve token usage. Use Haiku for mechanical stages (logging, formatting, simple extraction) and Sonnet for the rest.
- Opus or Fable is acceptable only as an advisor where needed: a senior reviewer, judge or verdict seat, never for bulk work such as planners, writers, fixers or scanners.
- Set `model` explicitly on every worker `agent()` call; do not let workers inherit the session model.

# Claude Code Game Studios -- Game Studio Agent Architecture

Indie game development managed through 49 coordinated Claude Code subagents.
Each agent owns a specific domain, enforcing separation of concerns and quality.

## Technology Stack

- **Engine**: Godot 4.7.2
- **Language**: GDScript
- **Version Control**: Git with trunk-based development
- **Build System**: SCons (engine), Godot Export Templates
- **Asset Pipeline**: Godot Import System + custom resource pipeline

> **Note**: Engine-specialist agents exist for Godot, Unity, and Unreal with
> dedicated sub-specialists. Use the set matching your engine.

## Project Structure

@.claude/docs/directory-structure.md

## Engine Version Reference

@docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md


## Technical Preferences

`project.yaml` at the repo root is the primary config store — engine, specialists,
naming, platform, performance, modes. Skills resolve it via `resolve_config`
(see `.claude/docs/config-resolution.md`).

`.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` is the **legacy fallback**, read on demand
when a key is absent from `project.yaml`. It is not imported here: before
`/setup-engine` runs it is almost entirely `[TO BE CONFIGURED]` placeholders, and
after it runs `project.yaml` holds the real values.

## Coordination Rules

@.claude/docs/coordination-rules.md

## Collaboration Protocol

**User-driven collaboration, not autonomous execution.**
Every task follows: **Question -> Options -> Decision -> Draft -> Approval**

- Agents MUST ask "May I write this to [filepath]?" before using Write/Edit tools
  (exempt: `active.md` appends, agent memory, a subagent's new file at the path
  its orchestrating skill named; see `.claude/rules/agent-memory.md`)
- Agents MUST show drafts or summaries before requesting approval
- Multi-file changes require explicit approval for the full changeset
- No commits without user instruction
- A skipped or dismissed question is not an answer: act on nothing, re-ask in
  plain text and wait
- Started outside this file's folder? Warn first: hooks, deny rules and the
  ask-first mode load only when Claude Code starts here

See `docs/COLLABORATIVE-DESIGN-PRINCIPLE.md` for full protocol and examples.

> **First session?** If the project has no engine configured and no game concept,
> run `/start` to begin the guided onboarding flow.

## Coding Standards

@.claude/docs/coding-standards.md

## Context Management

Read `.claude/docs/context-management.md` on demand — it is a reference, not
session context. Two of its conventions are load-bearing and cited by name
elsewhere in the repo, so they are restated here rather than lost:

- **`production/session-state/active.md` is the session checkpoint.** The file is
  the memory, not the conversation. Read it first after any compaction, crash, or
  `/clear`.
- **Helpers in `.claude/scripts/` emit observations, never verdicts.** A script
  that scores or judges will eventually contradict a mode or override it cannot
  see. (Cited by `artifact-check.sh` and `adr-dep-graph.sh`.)

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

# Godot Engine — Version Reference

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine Version** | Godot 4.7 |
| **Installed at pin time** | 4.7.2.stable.mono.official.ed1daf0bf (matches pin; probed 2026-10-25 at `C:/Users/dasbl/Documents/Godot/`). 4.6.2 standard is also installed, unused. |
| **Release Date** | June 2026 (latest patch: 4.7.2, August 2026) |
| **Project Pinned** | 2026-10-17 |
| **Last Docs Verified** | 2026-10-17 (release timeline and 4.7 changes); 2026-02-12 (4.4-4.6 content) |
| **LLM Knowledge Cutoff** | May 2025 |

## Knowledge Gap Warning

The LLM's training data likely covers Godot up to ~4.3. Versions 4.5, 4.6
and 4.7 were released after the cutoff and introduced significant changes that
the model does NOT know about; 4.4 came out shortly before it and may be thinly
covered. Always cross-reference this directory before suggesting Godot API calls.

## Installed-Version Gap Warning

The warning above is one-directional — it covers the **model** knowing less than
this pin. The reverse gap is real and `/setup-engine` §3 creates it deliberately
("pin the newer one and upgrade later"): this reference can sit **ahead of the
installed editor**, and an agent citing it correctly then emits APIs that do not
compile locally. **Check `Installed at pin time` above before trusting a
version-qualified claim** — `NOT DETERMINED` means the gap is unknown, not absent.

## Post-Cutoff Version Timeline

| Version | Release | Risk Level | Key Theme |
|---------|---------|------------|-----------|
| 4.5 | Sep 2025 | HIGH | Accessibility (AccessKit), variadic args, @abstract, shader baker, SMAA |
| 4.6 | Jan 2026 | HIGH | Jolt default, glow rework, D3D12 default on Windows, IK restored |
| 4.7 | Jun 2026 | HIGH | AreaLight3D, HDR output, Asset Store replaces the Asset Library, VirtualJoystick, Jolt soft-body and world-boundary changes, typed-return overrides |

## Before the Cutoff

4.4 (Mar 2025, Jolt option, FileAccess return types) predates the May 2025
cutoff; the Knowledge Gap Warning still applies to it.

Dates from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases, checked 2026-10-17:
4.4 Mar 3 2025, 4.5 Sep 15 2025, 4.6 Jan 26 2026, 4.7 Jun 18 2026, 4.7.2 Aug 18
2026. Migration guides and release notes: `breaking-changes.md` § Sources.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag
- [Consistency-check needs a confirming run](consistency-check-confirming-run.md) — owner+registry fixes leave leftovers in consumer GDDs; grep referenced_by docs, print patch counts

## Knowledge Gap Warning

The LLM's training data likely covers Godot up to ~4.3. Versions 4.5, 4.6
and 4.7 were released after the cutoff and introduced significant changes that
the model does NOT know about; 4.4 came out shortly before it and may be thinly
covered. Always cross-reference this directory before suggesting Godot API calls.

## Installed-Version Gap Warning

The warning above is one-directional — it covers the **model** knowing less than
this pin. The reverse gap is real and `/setup-engine` §3 creates it deliberately
("pin the newer one and upgrade later"): this reference can sit **ahead of the
installed editor**, and an agent citing it correctly then emits APIs that do not
compile locally. **Check `Installed at pin time` above before trusting a
version-qualified claim** — `NOT DETERMINED` means the gap is unknown, not absent.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag

# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.
