440	## Alternatives Considered
441	
442	### Alternative 1: One `Controller` node that reads devices, owns the state and draws the body

440	## Alternatives Considered
441	
442	### Alternative 1: One `Controller` node that reads devices, owns the state and draws the body
443	- **Description**: A single `Node2D` (or autoload) reads `Input`, holds facing, gait and carry in its own fields, and moves the sprite.
444	- **Pros**: Least code; no read views; no resync because there is no boundary.
445	- **Cons**: State lives in the scene tree, so a save cannot restore it and a MIRROR peer cannot draw a remote body from state; presentation would write the simulation (kernel H4); the simulation would depend on a `Node` (ADR-0010 `SIM-01`); input timing would be the scene's, not the tick's.
446	- **Rejection Reason**: Breaks three Foundation rules and the GDD's PC-1 rationale; the three-part split is the minimum that satisfies them.
447	
448	### Alternative 2: Fold the Controller Sim into Ship Body (one block, one hook)
449	- **Description**: Body owns intent, gait, facing and position; the Controller is only an Adapter and a Presenter.
450	- **Pros**: One fewer block and hook; no `controller.step` -> `body.integrate` ordering edge.
451	- **Cons**: Intent and facing are seat semantics (what the player asked for) read by Interaction, Attention, Horror and the HUD; position is a kinematic fact. Merging them couples every reader of the first to Body's schema and its restore rules, and the GDD rejected it for that reason (PC-1 rationale).
452	- **Rejection Reason**: Keeping the input record apart from the integrator keeps both restore contracts small; the cost is one hook edge, which the topo-sort already handles.
453	
454	### Alternative 3: The Controller owns position and calls the Layout projection
455	- **Description**: `controller.step` integrates the foot box against Layout's rectangles.
456	- **Pros**: One owner for "where the player is".
457	- **Cons**: Puts the Layout projection inside an input system; cannot own an actor that transfers between bodies (pod hop, detach) without learning Body's rebase rules; Horror's reuse of `LocomotionStep` would have to reach into the Controller.
458	- **Rejection Reason**: PC-14's reasons; the composite ship and the transfer mutators are Body's.
459	
460	### Alternative 4: Per-tick held-state commands instead of change-based intents
461	- **Description**: The Adapter submits the current octant and aim every tick; no change filter, no `last_acked`, no resync.
462	- **Pros**: Self-healing; no resync rule; the simulation can never disagree with the hands for more than a tick.
463	- **Cons**: A steady 60 or more commands a second against `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` and the `var_to_bytes` size check, for a state that is constant most of the time; the command log and the replay trace would be dominated by repeats; ADR-0002's coalescing exists for exactly the bursty case, not a firehose.
464	- **Rejection Reason**: Change-based submission with one resync rule has the same invariant (hands equal intent within a tick of `RUNNING`) at one fiftieth of the traffic, and the five triggers are all observable.
465	
466	### Alternative 5: Poll-only edges, or latch in `_unhandled_input`
467	- **Description**: Use `is_action_just_pressed` and `just_released` for every edge; or latch events in `_unhandled_input`.
468	- **Pros**: Poll-only is the simplest code and needs no ring. `_unhandled_input` leaves `Control`s first refusal.
469	- **Cons**: Probe 6: a same-frame press and release cannot be ordered by polling, which the latch-until-released, fresh-press and hold-cancel rules need. `_unhandled_input` misses an event a focused `Control` consumed, which would silently drop a MenuInput accept.
470	- **Rejection Reason**: Ordered edges from `_input`, plus a poll for continuous state, is the smallest scheme that is correct for all three; the cost is the `EdgeRing`.
471	
472	### Alternative 6: A custom binding layer instead of `InputMap`
473	- **Description**: The Adapter matches raw `InputEventKey`/`JoypadButton` records against its own table; no `InputMap` actions.
474	- **Pros**: No dependence on `InputMap` device semantics (probe 3); total control of conflicts and contexts.
475	- **Cons**: Re-implements modifier matching, axis deadzones, echo and per-device merging that the engine already provides; the HUD, Settings and accessibility screens would each need the custom layer; Godot's merging of devices per action (a held pad `interact` survives a touch of the mouse) would have to be rebuilt.
476	- **Rejection Reason**: `InputMap` with runtime registration, zero engine deadzone and the any-device wildcard gives the same control with the engine's matching; the pitfall (probe 3) is closed by one factory and one test.
477	
478	### Alternative 7: Mouse aim through the camera pose (`mouse_to_world_view`) or anchored on the avatar
479	- **Description**: Use the full `pose_q` inverse for aim, or measure aim from the drawn avatar position.
480	- **Pros**: Matches picking and pings; the anchored form holds the beam rigid against the hand.
481	- **Cons**: `pose_q` contains the look-ahead `L`, which is a function of aim, so a still cursor would drift the beam (a feedback loop with no cursor drawn to explain it). Anchoring on the avatar puts the hidden-cursor reference up to the follow lag plus the look-ahead off the drawn avatar (GDD PC-5, ruling R4).
482	- **Rejection Reason**: The open-loop `f_q` form is the ruled one and ADR-0008 publishes it; the lint `CTL-06` keeps the loop open.
483	
484	### Alternative 8: Identify devices by number (`device == 0`, or the `DEVICE_ID_*` constants)
485	- **Description**: Decide keyboard, mouse or pad from `event.device`.
486	- **Pros**: One integer compare.
487	- **Cons**: 4.7 changed the keyboard and mouse numbers and some pads already used 0 (`modules/input.md`); pads are numbered by enumeration order, so a pad that is not first matches nothing; a comparison with a constant bakes the engine's numbering into game code.
488	- **Rejection Reason**: Event type is stable across versions; the only legal numeric use is a variable holding the active pad's index, never a literal.
489	
490	### Alternative 9: Persist the context, `last_acked` and the pre-play ledger
491	- **Description**: Save Adapter state so a load resumes mid-intent.
492	- **Pros**: A restore could keep the exact held input.
493	- **Cons**: The hands are the source of truth, not the save; a persisted `last_acked` would claim the simulation holds a value it just lost; the context is presentation. It would also put device state into a hashed block.
494	- **Rejection Reason**: The restore normalises transient fields and the resync re-sends the real hands (TR-pc-021).
495	
496	## Consequences
497	
498	### Positive
499	- Only five files can read a device; every other Controller file is pure over ints, so the Adapter's logic is unit-testable with a scripted source and replayable from a recorded trace.
500	- The Adapter cannot write the simulation by construction (no `ModuleFacet`, a `PresentationFacet` of class `INPUT_SURFACE`, an import-edge matrix that stops at `views/`), and the Controller Sim cannot read a device (no `Input` token is legal under `src/sim/`).
501	- One field list drives the block, the view and the snapshot, so the three cannot drift; a new field is one edit and one failing test until the rest follow.
502	- The 4.7 device-id change is closed twice: by classification on event type and by a literal-compare lint; the wildcard binding closes the pad-index hazard the probes found.
503	- Resync is one mechanism with five labelled causes, all observable from the clock, the result ring, the notifications and Body's view, with no kernel hook.
504	- Hold, toggle, pad and keyboard policies differ only in when the Adapter submits two commands the owners already define.
505	- Intent submission is ten to fifty times lighter than per-tick held state and stays inside the 26 commands a second budget.
506	
507	### Negative
508	- Adapter state is lost on a restore and rebuilt from the hands; a player holding a key across a load gets one resend, at most one sub-pixel `sub` remainder, and no more.
509	- The Adapter reads the previous frame's `f_q` and layout (it runs before the pipeline), so aim and the zoom warp carry one frame of lag, and a warp frame drops one frame of mouse motion.
510	- Edge ordering needs an `EdgeRing` and a second path beside polling; the lint and fixtures to keep that honest are real work.
511	- The avatar's tick-stepped frames (idle, work, stagger, down) use the committed tick, an exception to a registry rule that must be defended in review and by test, because no lint can see it.
512	- Four Controller mutators are Class A in ADR-0003's vocabulary while the GDD says Class B; two documents must be amended.
513	- The Presenter and Audio share one pure function, which makes `AvatarFrames` a small cross-presentation contract that must stay stable.
514	
515	## Risks
516	- **R1. Process order on a release export is unverified (KRN-LAT-02).** If the Adapter does not run before the driver, an intent sampled in frame N lands a tick late. *Mitigation*: shared spike item (h); the Adapter's tests assert only the order of its own calls, and a one-tick-later landing degrades latency, not correctness.
517	- **R2. Warp, confinement and cursor units on a real letterboxed window.** If `warp_mouse` is not visible in the same frame, or emits a motion event, the zoom edge could nudge aim by a few units. *Mitigation*: PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (a), (b); the stored-`cursor_off` step already makes the warp frame independent of the OS read; acceptance of § 6.3 is gated on the spike.
518	- **R3. The `-1` wildcard may not match on a real SDL3 pad.** *Mitigation*: spike (f), (g); fallback is a per-device binding rebuilt on `joy_connection_changed`, behind `BindingFactory`, with no change to callers.
519	- **R4. `_input` plus `set_input_as_handled()` could collide with ADR-0030's focus design** (a `Control` expecting `ui_accept`). *Mitigation*: the layer is specified to take MenuInput only (TR-charttable-010); an amendment path is open (OQ-B); no `ui_*` action is read by gameplay or MenuInput.
520	- **R5. The registry exception for avatar tick-stepped loops** could be copied by other presenters. *Mitigation*: it is scoped to `AvatarFrames` and recorded as a foundation ask; ADR-0009's presenter tests assert that no other presenter reads `frame.T` for phase.
521	- **R6. PC-14 and the TR-pc-035 reading rest on ADR-0015.** If Body's transfer mutators do not reset `pos_prev` and `sub`, the arrival cell can be displaced. *Mitigation*: stated as an assumption on ADR-0015 and tested by the transfer property test (TR-shipbody-048).
522	- **R7. Frame-old `f_q`.** At a high turn rate while moving, aim could trail by up to the one-frame follow change. *Mitigation*: the GDD already bounds the follow term at 36 px and measures target acquisition in the motion-integrity spike; the Adapter does not add to the bound.
523	- **R8. Float `atan2` is not bit-identical across machines.** *Mitigation*: not claimed; the simulation replays the recorded submission log, and the Adapter-level trace test is per-machine.
524	- **R9. Solo detection for `give_up` is a row count.** If co-op seats exist without avatars, the count could mis-read. *Mitigation*: OQ-C; the check moves to a kernel session fact under ADR-0032.
525	- **R10. Action ids in rebinding files.** A renamed action would orphan a user override. *Mitigation*: stable integer ids with an append-only ledger (ADR-0007 § 3), names are display only.
526	- **R11. Touch, gyro and `VirtualJoystick` (4.7) are out of scope.** A later platform could need a fourth device class. *Mitigation*: `DeviceClass.OTHER` is ignored and adding a class is an enum append plus one classifier branch.

Now I'm going through several more cross-reference updates: adding a ledger citation to CT-20, a §7.1 sentence reference for ADR-0034's BodyScenes, confirming CT-54 keeps ADR-0019's get_ naming, and naming the ControllerCatalog table in CT-57. Finally I'm updating the registry candidates list — removing chest_sim/hand_sim in favor of describing chest and hand points as read-time scalar getters rather than stored state, updating controller_view's signal signature, and marking input_source_port's ten methods as abstract with typed returns.

Now I'm defining `RawEvent.classify` to tag InputEventJoypadMotion as CONTINUOUS_ONLY, with `is_edge_event` returning false for joypad and mouse motion, while mouse motion still generates pointer records. I'm planning to write the edits bottom-up through the file to avoid line-reference issues, starting with the Engine Compatibility probes table — replacing the deadzone-storage note with updated text plus new probes for `_input` delivery order and process_priority behavior — then moving to the Verification Required section, which requires matching the entire long line exactly for the replacement.

### Acceptance gates (one table; replaces three earlier statements that disagreed)

| Gate | Covers | Requires | Unblocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G-SIM** (sim half and the pure Adapter logic) | § 1, § 2, § 3.4 to § 3.6, § 3.8, § 3.9, § 4.1 to § 4.3, § 5, § 7 except the beam `Light2D` origin, § 8.2 to § 8.6 and every test of § 8.3 that runs on a `FakeInputSource`; no device hardware | The Foundation ADRs (0001 to 0005, 0008 to 0010) Accepted, KRN-LAT-02 passed (item (h) is shared with it), and ADR-0015 co-accepted (BodyView and ControllerView are mutual ports) | Every Interaction, Assembly, Body and Chart Table story that calls the Controller's mutators or reads its views |
| **G-DEVICE** (device-facing Adapter) | § 3.2 (latch), the § 3.3 wildcard and non-zero deadzone, § 3.7 focus, § 4.4 cursor, § 6 | PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 items marked **REQUIRED** below | Stories that touch `EngineInputSource`, `BindingFactory`, the cursor or aim sampling |
| **G-BEAM** (beam light origin) | The beam `Light2D` entry of § 7.1 and § 7.2 | ADR-0018 Accepted and ADR-0009 accepting `put_light_origin` (ADR-0018 OQ-A) | The Presenter's light-writing story only |

Spike items: **REQUIRED** for G-DEVICE are (a) cursor unit, (b) warp and confinement behaviour, and (h) process order on a release export, run on a keyboard, a mouse and one pad in a non-embedded window. **RECORDED** (the result is written down and relaxes or confirms later items; failure never blocks acceptance, and the fallback ships) are: (c) wheel burst (fallback: one zoom step per frame, § 6.4, already the rule); (d) real OS echo (fallback: the held-set drops a press for a control already held, § 3.2); (e) focus events (fallback: all three notifications feed one latch and the resync of trigger iv runs on any of them, § 3.7); (f) pad ids and the second, non-XInput pad (fallback: R3's per-device rebind on `joy_connection_changed`); (g) wildcard on every pad (fallback: R3); (i) AZERTY and QWERTZ labels (fallback: the `KeycapToken.UNKNOWN` keycap); and the RM-DECK runs of (a), (b), (e) (fallback: the virtual cursor of § 6.3 and the re-assert of § 4.4). The ADR header Status stays Proposed until the technical-director records acceptance; the technical-director may record G-SIM alone as the acceptance of the sim half and keep G-DEVICE and G-BEAM as annotations on the Status line (an annotation, not a new status value).

input.old_string: (10) `InputMap.add_action(name, 0.0)` stores a 0.0 deadzone. (11)
input.new_string: (10) `InputMap.add_action(name, 0.0)` stores a 0.0 deadzone (storage only; its behaviour is probe 13). (11)

input.old_string: (12) The root `Window` reports `content_scale_mode` 0 (disabled) in a bare `SceneTree` script. |
input.new_string: (12) The root `Window` reports `content_scale_mode` 0 (disabled) in a bare `SceneTree` script; this says nothing about the project, whose stretch setting ADR-0008 owns. **Engine-review re-probes (4.7.2 headless, 2026-10-29):** (13) **A 0.0 deadzone makes an action report pressed at rest.** With `add_action(name, 0.0)` an `InputEventJoypadMotion` with `axis_value` 0.0 reports `is_action_pressed` TRUE for both the positive and the negative direction action (`abs(0.0) >= 0.0`), a 0.02 value is also pressed, and a trigger axis at rest (0.0) reports its action pressed; `Input.is_action_pressed` goes true for both `mv_r` and `mv_l` after one centred-stick event while `get_action_raw_strength` correctly stays 0.0 (it ignores the deadzone). Successive 0.7 and 0.9 motion events each report pressed (a held stick is "pressed" on every motion event). Probe 13 is re-run with the revised non-zero registration (§ 3.3) as a headless assertion in the p1 script: a centred-stick event and a trigger-at-rest event make no catalogue action pressed. (14) `_input` is delivered in **reverse tree order** (a later sibling first), `process_priority` has no effect on `_input` order (two nodes, priorities swapped between runs), a handled event never reaches the earlier sibling, and `set_input_as_handled()` does not change `Input.*` poll state. (15) `set_input_as_handled()` is a `Viewport` method: a Node script calling it bare is a parse error ("Function not found in base self"); `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` compiles and works from `_input`. (16) `@abstract` before `class_name`/`extends` with `@abstract func ... -> T` bodies compiles; a subclass implementing only some abstract methods is a parse error. Those four re-probes are the engine review's result; probes 4, 5, 8, 9, 11 and 12 above were not re-run and are plausible. |

input.old_string: **PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (gates acceptance of §§ 3.2, 4.4 and 6, not the block, commands or hooks).** On a windowed 4.7.2 editor session and a release export, on a window whose picture is letterboxed at two zoom steps, with a keyboard, a mouse, an XInput pad and a non-XInput pad:
input.new_string: **PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (one gate table, "Acceptance gates" below; it gates the device-facing Adapter sections only, never the block, commands, hooks, mutators or views).** Run in a **non-embedded** window (the editor's embedded game window, 4.4+, may not honour confine or warp and would give false results) and on a release export, on a window whose picture is letterboxed at two zoom steps, with a keyboard, a mouse, an XInput pad and a non-XInput pad; items (a), (b) and (e) are also run on RM-DECK (Linux, and under gamescope if that is the shipped session), because the docs restrict `warp_mouse` to Windows, macOS and Linux and Wayland is a doubtful case:

input.old_string: (b) under `MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED_HIDDEN`, `warp_mouse` position is visible to `get_mouse_position` in the same frame or only the next, and whether it emits a synthetic `InputEventMouseMotion` (decides whether the Adapter must hold its own `cursor_off` through a warp frame, § 6.3); (c) how many wheel `InputEventMouseButton`s one frame can deliver for a notched and a high-resolution wheel, and their `factor`;
input.new_string: (b) under `MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED_HIDDEN`, `Input.warp_mouse` (window pixels, the one warp call used; `Viewport.warp_mouse` takes viewport coordinates and is not called) is a no-op or takes effect, its position is visible to `get_mouse_position` in the same frame or only the next, and whether it emits a synthetic `InputEventMouseMotion` (decides whether the Adapter must hold its own `cursor_off` through a warp frame, and whether the virtual-cursor fallback of § 6.3 is needed); also whether confinement survives focus loss and alt-tab (decides the re-assert rule of § 4.4); (c) how many wheel `InputEventMouseButton` **press** events one frame can deliver for a notched and a high-resolution wheel, and their `factor` (the paired releases are ignored, § 3.2);

input.old_string: and whether pressed actions stay pressed after the loss;
input.new_string: whether pressed actions stay pressed after the loss, and whether the engine's own focus-out release arrives as synthetic release events through `_input` (§ 3.7);

input.old_string: Every claim above that the 2026-10-29 probe list does not contain is UNVERIFIED until this spike records it. |
input.new_string:
Every claim above that the 2026-10-29 probe list does not contain is UNVERIFIED until this spike records it. |

### Acceptance gates (one table; replaces three earlier statements that disagreed)

| Gate | Covers | Requires | Unblocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G-SIM** (sim half and the pure Adapter logic) | § 1, § 2, § 3.4 to § 3.6, § 3.8, § 3.9, § 4.1 to § 4.3, § 5, § 7 except the beam `Light2D` origin, § 8.2 to § 8.6 and every test of § 8.3 that runs on a `FakeInputSource`; no device hardware | The Foundation ADRs (0001 to 0005, 0008 to 0010) Accepted, KRN-LAT-02 passed (item (h) is shared with it), and ADR-0015 co-accepted (BodyView and ControllerView are mutual ports) | Every Interaction, Assembly, Body and Chart Table story that calls the Controller's mutators or reads its views |
| **G-DEVICE** (device-facing Adapter) | § 3.2 (latch), the § 3.3 wildcard and non-zero deadzone, § 3.7 focus, § 4.4 cursor, § 6 | PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 items marked **REQUIRED** below | Stories that touch `EngineInputSource`, `BindingFactory`, the cursor or aim sampling |
| **G-BEAM** (beam light origin) | The beam `Light2D` entry of § 7.1 and § 7.2 | ADR-0018 Accepted and ADR-0009 accepting `put_light_origin` (ADR-0018 OQ-A) | The Presenter's light-writing story only |

Spike items: **REQUIRED** for G-DEVICE are (a) cursor unit, (b) warp and confinement behaviour, and (h) process order on a release export, run on a keyboard, a mouse and one pad in a non-embedded window. **RECORDED** (the result is written down and relaxes or confirms later items; failure never blocks acceptance, and the fallback ships) are: (c) wheel burst (fallback: one zoom step per frame, § 6.4, already the rule); (d) real OS echo (fallback: the held-set drops a press for a control already held, § 3.2); (e) focus events (fallback: all three notifications feed one latch and the resync of trigger iv runs on any of them, § 3.7); (f) pad ids and the second, non-XInput pad (fallback: R3's per-device rebind on `joy_connection_changed`); (g) wildcard on every pad (fallback: R3); (i) AZERTY and QWERTZ labels (fallback: the `KeycapToken.UNKNOWN` keycap); and the RM-DECK runs of (a), (b), (e) (fallback: the virtual cursor of § 6.3 and the re-assert of § 4.4). The ADR header Status stays Proposed until the technical-director records acceptance; the technical-director may record G-SIM alone as the acceptance of the sim half and keep G-DEVICE and G-BEAM as annotations on the Status line (an annotation, not a new status value).

input.new_string:
The block is a `RefCounted` holding one `ControllerRow` (a `RefCounted` with typed `int` fields, never a `Dictionary`) per PlayerId in an `Array[ControllerRow]` sorted by id. MVP has one row; the type allows four.

**Row lifecycle (T7).** `default_state(ctx)` returns the MVP payload: **one row for the host PlayerId at the rest values of § 2.2** (the PlayerId of the single seat Body binds at new game; the constant is ADR-0015's and ADR-0002's, an assumption), written through the same column encoder as `snapshot`, so a new game and a restore take the same path (ADR-0016 § default-state-through-restore). There is no other creation path at MVP: no command creates a row and no mutator of § 2.5 does. A VS-B seat created after new game (ADR-0032) would add a fifth published mutator (`ensure_row`) under that ADR's amendment; it is not built here. A seat bound in `body.state` with no `controller.state` row after restore is a restore fault `PC_ROW_MISSING` (local code 10, § 2.8), raised by ADR-0016's cross-block verifier (added to its verifier list as an assumption), not by `post_restore`, which therefore reads Suit only. At run time a missing row is not silent: `set_move_intent` and `set_aim` reject `NO_SEAT_ROW` (§ 2.3) and ADR-0015 counts `BDY_SEAT_UNBOUND` from `has_row(player_id)` (§ 2.6).

content.thinking: I'm thinking through section 2.1 - the restore_after row, its default state, and how the row behaves across its lifecycle for T7.

input.old_string: `restore` itself reads no other block (it validates into scratch), but `post_restore` reads both (chest and hand points from Body, the cap from Suit), and the kernel GDD orders
input.new_string: `restore` itself reads no other block (it validates into scratch), `post_restore` reads Suit's cap only (the chest and hand points are read-time getters, § 2.6, so nothing derived from Body is recomputed at restore), the `body.state` edge is kept so that the cross-block verifier checks of ADR-0016 (the `PC_ROW_MISSING` seat check of § 2.1, the `carry_ref` check of § 2.7) see Body restored first and ADR-0016 may drop it, and the kernel GDD orders

input.old_string: The block is a `RefCounted` holding one `ControllerRow` (a `RefCounted` with typed `int` fields, never a `Dictionary`) per PlayerId in an `Array[ControllerRow]` sorted by id. MVP has one row; the type allows four.
input.new_string:
The block is a `RefCounted` holding one `ControllerRow` (a `RefCounted` with typed `int` fields, never a `Dictionary`) per PlayerId in an `Array[ControllerRow]` sorted by id. MVP has one row; the type allows four.

**Row lifecycle (T7).** `default_state(ctx)` returns the MVP payload: **one row for the host PlayerId at the rest values of § 2.2** (the PlayerId of the single seat Body binds at new game; the constant is ADR-0015's and ADR-0002's, an assumption), written through the same column encoder as `snapshot`, so a new game and a restore take the same path (ADR-0016 § default-state-through-restore). There is no other creation path at MVP: no command creates a row and no mutator of § 2.5 does. A VS-B seat created after new game (ADR-0032) would add a fifth published mutator (`ensure_row`) under that ADR's amendment; it is not built here. A seat bound in `body.state` with no `controller.state` row after restore is a restore fault `PC_ROW_MISSING` (local code 10, § 2.8), raised by ADR-0016's cross-block verifier (added to its verifier list as an assumption), not by `post_restore`, which therefore reads Suit only. At run time a missing row is not silent: `set_move_intent` and `set_aim` reject `NO_SEAT_ROW` (§ 2.3) and ADR-0015 counts `BDY_SEAT_UNBOUND` from `has_row(player_id)` (§ 2.6).

input.old_string: | `player_id` | int, row key | `default_state`, seat creation | live | yes |
input.new_string: | `player_id` | int, row key | `default_state` (MVP: the one host row, § 2.1 row lifecycle); VS-B seat creation is ADR-0032's | live | yes |

input.old_string:
| `chest_sim`, `hand_sim` | two ints each | **derived** each step and in `post_restore` | never persisted, never hashed | yes (chest, hand points) |

`cap_seen` persists so that a restore never re-fires the cap falling edge; `post_restore` additionally re-reads Suit's cap and sets `cap_seen := cap`, which equals the restored `suit.state` value and is a no-op for the round trip (PC-9, PC-17). The derived chest and hand points live on the row as a cache excluded from the payload, so the canonical state hash (which is taken over the snapshot payload, ADR-0005) never sees them.
input.new_string:
*There is no `chest_sim` / `hand_sim` field (CT-28).* The chest and hand points are not stored on the row, in the payload, or anywhere; § 2.6 publishes them as read-time getters. A stored value written in `controller.step` (which runs before `body.integrate`) would be one tick stale against the foot origin that ADR-0017 and ADR-0018 read after `body.integrate`.

`cap_seen` persists so that a restore never re-fires the cap falling edge; `post_restore` re-reads Suit's cap and sets `cap_seen := cap`, which equals the restored `suit.state` value and is a no-op for the round trip (PC-9, PC-17). That is the whole of `post_restore` (ADR-0016 V8 becomes "derived recompute of `cap_seen` only").

input.old_string: Getters are keyed by PlayerId and return scalars or fill a caller-owned buffer: `octant`, `run`, `gait_effective`, `aim_angle`, `aim_live`, `facing`, `loco_state`, `carry_ref`, `salvage_carry`, `channel_ref(out)`, `channel_face`, `chest_point`, `hand_point`, `intent_octant` and `intent_run` (the owners' `validate` reads `intent_octant`, PC-7), `row_count`. The accessors follow ADR-0010's `get_<noun>` rule where a bare name would shadow a native method. **Attention and Horror read only `loco_state`:** `ControllerView` is one facade (ADR-0003 § 7 issues one view per block), so the restriction is a lint, `CTL-05`: in `src/sim/attention/` and `src/sim/horror/` the only `ControllerView` member name that may appear is `loco_state`. input.new_string:
Getters are keyed by PlayerId and return scalars or fill a caller-owned buffer. Every `published` field of § 2.2 has a `get_<noun>(player_id)` getter (the complete signatures are in Key Interfaces): `get_octant`, `get_intent_octant`, `get_intent_run` (the GDD's "run"; the block has no separate `run` field), `get_gait_effective`, `get_aim_angle`, `get_aim_live`, `get_facing`, `get_loco_state`, `get_carry_ref`, `get_salvage_carry`, `get_channel_ref(player_id, out)`, `get_channel_face`, `get_stagger_end_tick`, `get_t_downed`, the four point getters below, and the non-field accessors `has_row(player_id) -> bool` (ADR-0015 consumes it for `BDY_SEAT_UNBOUND`), `row_count()` (kept for the `give_up` solo test) and `is_empty()`. One style throughout (ADR-0010 accessor naming, CT-54): `get_<noun>` for per-seat values, and the three named non-field accessors above. The owners' `validate` reads `intent_octant` (PC-7).

**The chest and hand points (CT-28; TR-pc-017).** `get_chest_x(player_id)`, `get_chest_y(player_id)`, `get_hand_x(player_id)` and `get_hand_y(player_id)` each return an `int`: an **absolute integer point in the body frame**, equal to `BodyView.pos_x(actor)` (or `pos_y`) plus `CHEST_POINT[sheet][row]` (or `HAND_POINT`), the offset's x mirrored by `facing` under the GDD's flip rule, where `actor = actor_of_seat(player_id)`, `row` is taken from the published `loco_state` through the table's `row_of_loco_state` map, and `sheet` is the catalogue's single MVP avatar sheet (a per-seat sheet would be a new persisted column and is not decided here, OQ-G). The getter is **O(1) and allocation-free**, computed on every read from the same tick's `pos_curr` that `body.integrate` just wrote, so the point cannot lag the foot origin: ADR-0017 D5.3 reads the apex as `get_chest_x/get_chest_y` in `emitter.place` (after `body.integrate`) and ADR-0018 reads the foot cell from `BodyView.pos_x/pos_y`, and the two agree by construction. Scalars in (`pos_x/pos_y`) and scalars out; no `Vector2i` is built on the per-tick Emitter path, as a style choice (ADR-0010 § 5.5 does not ban `Vector2i`; SIM-03 is not the reason). `CHEST_POINT` and `HAND_POINT` come from a **frozen ADR-0007 sim table, `ControllerCatalog` (loaded at pipeline stage 1), injected through `ControllerTuning`**; the § 7.3 presentation sidecar and its bounds checks read that same table, so there is one source of the offsets. Unit test (T1): on a moving tick, the apex used by `emitter.place` minus the chest offset for the tick's `(sheet, row)` equals that tick's `pos_curr`.

**Who reads what.** **Attention and Horror read only `loco_state`:** `ControllerView` is one facade (ADR-0003 § 7 issues one view per block), so the restriction is a lint, `CTL-05`: in `src/sim/attention/` and `src/sim/horror/` the only `ControllerView` member name that may appear is `get_loco_state`. **Body reads `octant` and `gait_effective` only** (ADR-0015, TR-shipbody-016; Body refuses `intent_octant`); Suit reads nothing; Interaction and Assembly read `intent_octant`, `loco_state`, `carry_ref`, `channel_ref` (they remain `intent_octant`'s readers); the Emitter (ADR-0017) reads the chest point, `aim_angle` and `loco_state`.

content.thinking:
I need to revise section 3.2 with targeted replacements rather than rewriting the whole paragraph, since matching the exact original text is tricky given its length. I'm identifying specific phrases to swap out, like the description of input event types and how they're resolved via action resolution, mouse wheel direction, pointer events, device class, and key echo handling.

I also want to add that the Adapter marks events as handled immediately after converting them to MenuInput, preventing double-processing by Controls, note the pad-axis behavior on EdgeRing overflow, and clarify that `_process` drains the ring while polling continuous action strength for movement, aim, and stick inputs.

input.old_string: a press or release of a registered action (resolved with `InputMap.event_is_action`, never by device number), a mouse wheel notch with its sign, a pointer move or button for MenuInput, the device class of the event (§ 3.3), and key echo (recorded and ignored). It submits nothing and writes nothing else (ADR-0001 § 3: `_input` may latch, only `_process` submits). `_process` drains the ring and polls `get_action_raw_strength` for the continuous families (move, aim keys, sticks).
input.new_string:
a press or release of a registered action **from a key, a mouse button or a pad button event** (resolved with `InputMap.event_is_action`, never by device number), a wheel step (below), a pointer move or button for MenuInput (a move record carries the integer `relative`, for the virtual cursor of § 6.3), the device class of the event (§ 3.3), and key echo (recorded and ignored). Records for a control are de-duplicated against an Adapter **held-set**: a press for a control already held adds no record. It submits nothing and writes nothing else (ADR-0001 § 3: `_input` may latch, only `_process` submits). `_process` drains the ring and polls `get_action_raw_strength` for the continuous families (move, aim keys, sticks, triggers).

**Pad axes are continuous-only (E4; probe 13).** `InputEventJoypadMotion` makes `is_action_pressed` true on *every* motion event while the stick is past the engine's threshold, so recording it would put a duplicate "press" per motion event per axis per frame into the ring and never a release (an overflow and ordering hazard; `PC_EDGE_OVERFLOW` would become the normal path while a stick is held). `RawEvent.classify` therefore marks `InputEventJoypadMotion` **continuous-only: it produces no edge record** (it still classifies as `DeviceClass.PAD`). Every stick and trigger edge (NAV directions, `MOVE_DEADZONE` crossings, a trigger-bound action) is derived in the Adapter, once per frame, from `get_action_raw_strength` with the existing hysteresis (`MOVE_DEADZONE`, `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`), and enters the same ordered stream at the frame's end. Edge records exist for key, mouse-button and pad-button events only.

**Wheel (E7).** A wheel is an `InputEventMouseButton` (`WHEEL_UP` / `WHEEL_DOWN`) delivered as a press immediately followed by a release; wheel events are not coalesced by `use_accumulated_input`, a high-resolution wheel or precision touchpad reports a fractional `factor`, and `WHEEL_LEFT` / `WHEEL_RIGHT` also exist. The latch counts **only `pressed == true` `WHEEL_UP` / `WHEEL_DOWN` events**, sums their signs into the frame's `wheel_net`, ignores the paired release, ignores `factor` (one zoom step per frame is already the cap, § 6.4) and ignores the horizontal buttons. `InputEventPanGesture` and `InputEventMagnifyGesture` classify as `OTHER` and are ignored: **on a touchpad, two-finger scroll and pinch do not zoom at MVP**; zoom there goes through the keys or pad d-pad (a driver that synthesises wheel buttons will work; that is UNVERIFIED). The burst size per frame is recorded by spike item (c).

content.thinking: I should check steps 1 and 3 in section 6.1, the virtual cursor behavior in 6.3, and the wheel interaction described in 6.4.

input.old_string: 3. `r = world - Vector2(floor(pos_curr) + Vector2i(0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y))` with `pos_curr` from Body's published view (the committed tick's position).
input.new_string: 3. `r = world - Vector2(float(px), float(py + AIM_ORIGIN_Y))` with `px = BodyView.pos_x(actor)` and `py = BodyView.pos_y(actor)` (ADR-0015's scalar getters; the committed tick's integer position, so no `floor` is needed). A `Vector2i` is built only here at the Adapter boundary, and only if a call needs one (CT-27).

input.old_string: and warps the hidden cursor to `picture_centre_new + cursor_off * k_new` (clamped to the window), so `aim_q` is unchanged within one unit while the avatar is still.
input.new_string: and warps the hidden cursor with `Input.warp_mouse` (window pixels; the one warp call, never `Viewport.warp_mouse`, whose coordinates are viewport coordinates and equal window pixels only because the root has no stretch) to `picture_centre_new + cursor_off * k_new` (clamped to the window), so `aim_q` is unchanged within one unit while the avatar is still.

input.old_string:
if the warped position is readable immediately the "use the stored offset" step is dropped.
- **Handover to the mouse.**
input.new_string:
if the warped position is readable immediately the "use the stored offset" step is dropped.
- **Fallback when `warp_cursor` is a no-op (E5).** `warp_mouse` is documented only for Windows, macOS and Linux, Wayland is doubtful, and RM-DECK is Linux. If a warp frame reads the position back more than `WARP_READBACK_TOLERANCE_PX` (a `ControllerTuning` knob, set from spike item (b)) from the target with no synthetic motion event, the Adapter latches **virtual-cursor mode** for the session: it keeps the stored `cursor_off` as a virtual cursor (the intended warp target, then advanced each frame by the summed integer `InputEventMouseMotion.relative` of that frame's pointer-move records, clamped to the window) and uses it in place of the OS read. Zoom and the handover warp then depend on no warp at all. Both modes feed the same `aim_q` computation.
- **Handover to the mouse.**

input.old_string: The wheel notches latched in a frame are summed to a net sign and the Adapter calls
input.new_string: The wheel steps latched in a frame (`pressed == true` `WHEEL_UP` / `WHEEL_DOWN` only, § 3.2) are summed to a net sign and the Adapter calls

input.old_string: the root viewport's mouse position, converted once with `floori` per axis
input.new_string: the root viewport's mouse position (in virtual-cursor mode, § 6.3, the virtual position), converted once with `floori` per axis

369	**8.3 Behavioural tests (gdUnit4, headless, a `FakeInputSource`).** One test per row of the context return table; the context matrix completeness check; octant and aim quantiser vectors including the lower half-plane; the send predicate and the 26 commands a second bound; the resync with each of the five triggers (and the labelled counter); a press during a channel is submitted and answered `BUSY` with nothing queued; `set_move_intent` before any command in one frame; a stop and a `begin_*` in one frame; focus loss and pad loss; the console seam with and without a pick; `tool_cycle` with two presses in one frame; the confirm bar under a 1 s frame, under `PAUSED` and across a pause; `BindingFactory` output has `device == BINDING_ANY_DEVICE` on every event; the field-agreement test of § 8.4; `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` byte identity from every rest value and from a live DOWNED row; a restore with the cap at WALK_ONLY does not stagger; the `FULL -> NONE -> WALK_ONLY -> FULL -> WALK_ONLY` sequence staggers once; the `controller.step` order tests; `Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED)` for a foreign actor; a DEAD seat rejects every Controller command and the Adapter submits nothing.
370	
371	**8.4 The field-agreement test (TR-pc-037).** One test iterates `ControllerSchema.fields()` and asserts: (a) every field has a typed member on `ControllerRow`; (b) the set of `snapshot` payload keys equals the set of fields with `persisted` true, by name and order; (c) every field with `published` true has a getter on `ControllerView` and every getter maps to a field; (d) `restore` rejects a payload missing any persisted column or carrying an extra one; (e) the Adapter classes name none of the persisted fields (so no Adapter-local datum can enter the block, TR-pc-021). Adding a field means editing the one list and the test fails until all four agree.
372	
373	**8.5 The input-trace format (TR-pc-039, replay half).** An `InputTrace` (`src/presentation/controller/input/input_trace.gd`, recorded only under the dev feature tag; replayed by `FakeInputSource`) is a text file of integer records, one line per rendered frame, committed under `tests/fixtures/controller/traces/` and immutable once committed. Header: a format version and the tick-rate name. Per frame: the injected `delta_us` (ADR-0001/ADR-0005's replay injection), the integer action strengths in `ANALOG_UNITS`, the ordered edge records of that frame (`action_id`, pressed, device class, echo), the wheel net sign, the cursor `Vector2i`, the pipeline values the Adapter read (`layout_version`, `f_q`, `k_z`, picture rect), the kernel state and `load_seq`, the focus flag and the pad-connected flag. Because every input is an int, the same trace through the same Adapter build yields the same submissions; `atan2` is not claimed bit-identical across machines, so the simulation's replay uses the **recorded submission log** (`(at_tick, type, payload, actor, correlation)`), not a re-run Adapter. **Cadence invariance (30, 60, 120, 144 fps):** device events carry the `at_tick` of the tick in whose P1 batch they must land, restricted to multiples of the least common multiple of the four frame periods in ticks (10), and the harness delivers each in the last frame before that tick, so every cadence can honour every event; the submission logs, the `controller.state` and `body.state` hashes and the Presenter's per-tick samples (frame, flip, integer position, light rotation, driven by an injected `PresentFrame` at alpha 1.0 at each tick) must match across the four cadences, across calm, tell, breach and sanity-stage read-view fixtures, and with `aim_indicator` on and off. Per-frame placements vary with alpha by design (ADR-0009). Hold-to-confirm timings are render-time by D.10 and are excluded from the identical claim: a confirm submit may land one frame apart across cadences.
374	
375	**8.6 Budgets (TR-pc-029).** Advisory, measured by the diagnostics timer on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, 120-frame warm-up, owned by the technical-director and living in `tests/performance/controller/`; a miss logs and never fails a logic test: Adapter at most 0.1 ms per frame (sampling, quantising, focus scoring over 32 candidates, submitting); `LocomotionStep` at most 0.05 ms per actor per tick against 2,000 rects (Body's, ADR-0015); `controller.step` at most 0.02 ms per actor per tick; Avatar Presenter at most 0.1 ms per avatar per frame; the `PC_*` diagnostics at most 0.01 ms per tick (dev only).

input.new_string: `InputMap` with runtime registration, a **non-zero** engine deadzone (a 0.0 deadzone makes a centred stick report pressed, probe 13; the gameplay deadzones are Adapter scalings over `get_action_raw_strength`, which ignores the engine deadzone) and the any-device wildcard gives the same control with the engine's matching; the pitfalls (probes 3 and 13) are closed by one factory and its tests.

input.old_string: - **R4. `_input` plus `set_input_as_handled()` could collide with ADR-0030's focus design** (a `Control` expecting `ui_accept`). *Mitigation*: the layer is specified to take MenuInput only (TR-charttable-010); an amendment path is open (OQ-B); no `ui_*` action is read by gameplay or MenuInput.
input.new_string: - **R4. `_input` plus `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` could collide with ADR-0030's focus design** (a `Control` expecting `ui_accept`), and `_input` order is tree order (probe 14), so any later node that handles an event first starves the ring. *Mitigation*: the ADR-0009 `INPUT_SURFACE` last-child rule, the boot assertion and the two-node test (§ 3.1); the layer is specified to take MenuInput only (TR-charttable-010); an amendment path is open (OQ-B); no `ui_*` action is read by gameplay or MenuInput. Cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0030 and ADR-0031: no `_input` or `set_input_as_handled()` in their layers; they consume MenuInput and `DevInputSink` through the Adapter; their Controls set `focus_mode` NONE unless exempted through the OQ-B `TextEntryProbe` port.

input.old_string: *Mitigation*: PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (a), (b); the stored-`cursor_off` step already makes the warp frame independent of the OS read; acceptance of § 6.3 is gated on the spike.
input.new_string: *Mitigation*: PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (a), (b) in a non-embedded window and on RM-DECK (Linux); the stored-`cursor_off` step already makes the warp frame independent of the OS read, and the virtual-cursor fallback of § 6.3 removes the dependence on `warp_mouse` altogether; the cursor mode is re-asserted on focus return (§ 4.4); acceptance of § 6.3 is gated on (a) and (b) only (gate G-DEVICE).

Each ask names its target, section and the exact sentence; the targets edit their own text.

These rows all check out fine. Now I'm reviewing the CPU performance note about `_input` calling event_is_action per registered action across key, mouse-button, and pad events, making sure the wording is accurate.

I'm also working through the Migration Plan rewrite, adding Foundation asks and Cross-ADR assumptions, updating the Validation Criteria and Related sections, revising OQ-B, adding OQ-G, and updating the Review Log.

input.old_string: `_input` does one `InputMap.event_is_action` per registered action for key, button and pad events (a few dozen compares, no allocation) and none for mouse motion.
input.new_string: `_input` does one `InputMap.event_is_action` per registered action for key, mouse-button and pad-button events (a few dozen compares, no allocation) and none for mouse motion or pad-axis motion (which records nothing). The four point getters are O(1) integer arithmetic over `BodyView.pos_x/pos_y` and a table row, allocation-free; their cost is charged inside the caller's budget (the Emitter's `EXPOSURE_BUDGET_MS`, the Presenter's 0.1 ms), not a separate line.

input.new_string:
- Foundation asks (below): ADR-0001 and ADR-0009 (cosmetic-phase exception; `AdapterViews` as an input-phase product; `_input` order and the last-child rule), ADR-0008 (`f_q` read accessor), ADR-0007 (the `ControllerCatalog` table), ADR-0010 (rule inventory rows), `tr-registry.yaml` wording.
- **Spike-list sync (as ADR-0005 does for its spikes), with the user's approval:** add PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 to `docs/architecture/architecture.md` § Spikes that gate ADRs and to the spike order after KRN-LAT-02; this ADR edits neither.

### Foundation asks
Each ask names its target, section and the exact sentence; the targets edit their own text.
1. **ADR-0001 / ADR-0009 and the registry pattern `cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter`** (registry owned by ADR-0001 and ADR-0009). Add the exception clause: "*Exception (ADR-0019 § 7.1): `AvatarFrames` in `src/presentation/controller/avatar/` may derive the avatar's tick-stepped loop frames (idle, work, stagger, down) from the committed tick `T` and a sim-held entry tick; no other presenter may read `frame.T` for phase.*" The entry gains `referenced_by: ADR-0019`. ADR-0009's presenter tests keep asserting the "no other presenter" half.
2. **ADR-0009 § 3 (stage-order rule "never read a product of the same or a later stage")**. Add: "*`INPUT_ADAPTER` precedes stage 0. `AdapterViews` is an INPUT_ADAPTER-phase product published before `PipelineRoot._process` and may be read by any stage (AVATAR, HUD, INSTRUMENTS, AUDIO).*"
3. **ADR-0001 § 3 item 3b and ADR-0009 (`INPUT_SURFACE` registration)**. Add to ADR-0001: "*`_input` is delivered in reverse tree order before the frame's `_process`; `process_priority` orders `_process` only.*" Add to ADR-0009: "*The composition root adds the `INPUT_SURFACE` node as the last child of its parent so its `_input` runs first; a boot assertion checks it.*"
4. **ADR-0008 § 3.3**. Add: "*`PipelineRoot` exposes the previous frame's `f_q`, `layout` and `layout_version` through read accessors callable from any node at any process priority; the values change only inside `PipelineRoot._process`.*"
5. **ADR-0007 (data domains)**. Register the frozen sim table `ControllerCatalog` (stage 1) holding `CHEST_POINT[sheet][row]`, `HAND_POINT[sheet][row]`, `row_of_loco_state` and the single MVP `sheet`, injected through `ControllerTuning`, with the structural invariants `abs(CHEST_POINT.x) <= 2` and `abs(HAND_POINT.x) <= 12` (CT-57).
6. **ADR-0010 § 6 rule inventory.** Add rows `CTL-01` to `CTL-09` and `CTL-11` to `CTL-13` of § 8.2 under the pack `controller_lint.gd`, the `READ-01` entry `tools/lint/config/allowlists/input_surface.json` with the symbol list of § 8.1 including `set_input_as_handled`, `warp_mouse`, `get_mouse_position`, `joy_connection_changed`, `focus_exited` and the two focus notification constants, per-file.
7. **`docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml` wording.** TR-pc-018: "Class B mutators" becomes "Class A status-returning mutators". TR-pc-035: "`controller.step` sets `pos_prev == pos_curr` and resets `sub`" becomes "`controller.step` clears `channel_ref`, `channel_face` and `channel_body` only; Body's transfer mutators (BM4 new side, BM5) set `pos_prev := pos_curr` and zero `sub`". TR-pc-046: the numeric bounds name sheet and row (the table has no frame dimension). TR-pc-017 lists the getters of Key Interfaces.
8. **ADR-0003 P3 share ledger (CT-20).** Row for this ADR: `controller.step` 0.02 ms per actor, 0.16 ms for eight, pending S1.

### Cross-ADR assumptions
- **ADR-0015** (co-accepted): `BodyView.pos_x/pos_y(actor)`, `body_of_actor`, `actor_of_seat`, `seat_of_actor`, `moved(actor)`; BM3/BM4/BM5 as in § 1.3; Body reads only `octant` and `gait_effective`; it consumes `has_row` for `BDY_SEAT_UNBOUND`.
- **ADR-0016**: V7 (`carry_ref` equals Suit's carried id, or both NONE) and, if ADR-0020 accepts it, V11; V8 is "derived recompute of `cap_seen` only"; the seat-row check `PC_ROW_MISSING`; KRN-RST-05 states the § 8.5 input model.
- **ADR-0017**: D5.3 and its ADR-0019 assumption row use exactly `get_chest_x/get_chest_y`, `get_aim_angle` and `get_loco_state`; D13.1 reads "no `Vector2i` in the persisted payload (ADR-0006), and none in the view surface as a style choice (scalar getters, no allocation)"; the SIM-03 citation is removed.
- **ADR-0018**: owns the shadow-origin rule (mode B) and `put_light_origin`; its § 4.1 places the beam `Light2D` under the translation-only BodyRoot of `body_of_actor(actor)` through `BodyScenes` LIGHTING.
- **ADR-0020**: publishes the candidate query, the channel start tick, the instance counter and V11 acceptance. **ADR-0022**: publishes the Attention mutator class name and the `push_stimulus` signature (§ 2.4). **ADR-0026** (not on disk): `is_pod_body(body_id) -> bool` and `home_body`. **ADR-0023**: Horror rigs call `BodyScenes.rebind(node, body_id, section_id)` when their section changes. **ADR-0030 and ADR-0031** (not on disk): no `_input` or `set_input_as_handled()` in their layers; they consume MenuInput and `DevInputSink` through the Adapter; their Controls set `focus_mode` NONE unless exempted through the OQ-B `TextEntryProbe` port. **ADR-0034**: `BodyScenes.attach_presenter` and the stage-0 `reparent(p, false)` of the Presenter node and every LIGHTING node of an actor on `BODY_TRANSFER` (§ 7.1).

registry_candidates.name: input_sampling_and_edges
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: input_sampling_and_edges
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed
    api: "InputAdapter._input (added as the LAST child of its parent so it runs first; _input order is reverse tree order, process_priority does not affect it) latches ordered press/release records for key, mouse-button and pad-button events, wheel presses (pressed==true WHEEL_UP/DOWN only) and pointer events into a preallocated EdgeRing de-duplicated against a held-set, and submits nothing; InputEventJoypadMotion is continuous-only (no edge record); InputAdapter._process (INPUT_ADAPTER -100) drains the ring, polls Input.get_action_raw_strength for continuous families, derives stick and trigger edges once per frame with hysteresis, and is the only place submit() is called, in the order set_move_intent, set_aim, commands; the Adapter uses _input (not _unhandled_input) and is the only caller of get_viewport().set_input_as_handled() for action-bound events"
    not: "polling just_pressed/just_released alone (a same-frame press and release cannot be ordered, probed 2026-10-29); _unhandled_input latching; recording pad-axis motion as edges; calling set_input_as_handled as a Node method (it is Viewport's); _input or set_input_as_handled in any layer, HUD or debug overlay; submit from _input, a signal handler or _physics_process; input buffering (ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS 0)"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    reason: "Ordered edges are needed by latch-until-released, fresh-press and hold-cancel rules; a focused Control would otherwise consume a press before _unhandled_input; a later node handling an event first would starve the ring; pad-axis motion reports pressed on every event; one tick of latency"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: "2026-10-29 (review: E2, E3, E4, E7)"

registry_candidates.name: existing_entries_cited_by_adr_0019
registry_candidates.entry_yaml: Append docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md to referenced_by of these existing entries: interfaces command_submission, zoom_request, render_layout, presentation_facet, presentation_stage_order; api_decisions frame_order, lint_forbidden_token_list, source_layout; forbidden_patterns presentation_submit_without_handle, command_constructed_outside_kernel; interfaces owner_callable_contract and mutator_status (the four Controller mutators are Class A); forbidden_patterns cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter, which also gains the exception clause 'AvatarFrames in src/presentation/controller/avatar/ may derive the avatar's tick-stepped loop frames (idle, work, stagger, down) from the committed tick T and a sim-held entry tick; no other presenter may read frame.T for phase' (owned by ADR-0001/ADR-0009, see Foundation asks 1); also referenced_by for the ADR-0018 beam light allow-list entry (put_light_origin) and the ADR-0015 BodyView position getters.

gdd_sync.new: through four published status-returning mutators (Class A in ADR-0003's taxonomy: each has a `check_*` twin and returns OK, REFUSED or -fault_code; ADR-0019 § 2.5)

gdd_sync.old: **→ ADR** (InputMap vs a custom binding layer; edge detection by event vs polling).
gdd_sync.new: **Decided in ADR-0019 § 3.2 and § 3.3**: `InputMap` actions registered at runtime from data with a non-zero engine deadzone, the any-device wildcard and `physical_keycode`; ordered edges latched in `_input` (key, mouse-button and pad-button events only; pad-axis motion is continuous) and continuous state polled in `_process`; devices identified by event type.

gdd_sync.old: the engine's echo flag is **[UNV]** until the ADR spike
gdd_sync.new: probed 2026-10-29 on 4.7.2: a synthetic echo event does not re-fire `is_action_just_pressed`; real OS key repeat is still **[UNV]** until PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (d), a RECORDED item with a held-set fallback

gdd_sync.old: THEN** the Suit read it requests is `locomotion_cap` only and never Suit's internal vitals ladder.
gdd_sync.new: THEN** the Suit reads it requests are `locomotion_cap` and `stowed_heavy` only (TR-suit-033) and never Suit's internal vitals ladder.

gdd_sync.old: Derived (idle breathing, tick-stepped) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `frame_idle = posmod(floor((T − T_enter) / IDLE_FRAME_TICKS), 6)`
gdd_sync.new: Derived (idle breathing, tick-stepped) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; free-running from the committed tick, ADR-0019 § 7.1)*: `frame_idle = posmod(floor(T / IDLE_FRAME_TICKS), 6)`

gdd_sync.old: Either the Adapter hands the cursor position and zoom edges to the pipeline root, or the lint carries an allow-list naming the pipeline root.
gdd_sync.new: Resolved by ADR-0019 § 6.4 and § 8.1: the Adapter owns every Input read, the pipeline root reads none, zoom edges reach it by `request_zoom_step` and the cursor is published as `AdapterViews.get_cursor_px()`; the lint carries an allow-list of the Adapter's registered files. (Earlier text:) Either the Adapter hands the cursor position and zoom edges to the pipeline root, or the lint carries an allow-list naming the pipeline root.

decisions.chosen: Named non-zero ENGINE_ACTION_DEADZONE (0.2 in the interface sketch, 0.5 also legal); MOVE/AIM_DEADZONE stay Adapter scalings over get_action_raw_strength; boot lint rejects 0.0
decisions.reason: A 0.0 deadzone makes a centred stick and a resting trigger report pressed (probed); get_action_raw_strength ignores the deadzone so raw strength stays raw

decisions.chosen: Read-time scalar getters (get_chest_x/y, get_hand_x/y -> int) over BodyView.pos_x/pos_y plus a frozen ControllerCatalog table keyed [sheet][row], row from loco_state; nothing stored; post_restore recomputes cap_seen only
decisions.reason: A derived value stored in controller.step is one tick stale against body.integrate; read-time cannot lag and matches the binding ruling

decisions.chosen: Beam position via Placement.put_light_origin at the foot cell plus CELL_CENTRE (ADR-0018 mode B); chest is cone apex only; ADR-0018 cited under Related, not Depends On
decisions.reason: ADR-0018 owns the rule; listing it in Depends On would form a 0019 -> 0018 -> 0017 -> 0019 cycle

decisions.chosen: One gate table: G-SIM (Foundation ADRs, KRN-LAT-02, ADR-0015 co-acceptance), G-DEVICE (spike a, b, h REQUIRED), G-BEAM (ADR-0018); other spike items RECORDED with named fallbacks; Status stays Proposed with an optional Status-line annotation for split acceptance
decisions.reason: The sim half needs no device hardware and should not wait on an XInput pad, a non-XInput pad and display-scaling runs

decisions.chosen: InputEventJoypadMotion classified continuous-only with no ring record; stick and trigger edges derived in the Adapter from get_action_raw_strength with hysteresis, once per frame
decisions.reason: is_action_pressed is true on every motion event past the threshold, which would flood the ring and never produce a release

decisions.chosen: Adapter is the last child so its _input runs first; boot assertion plus two-node test; only the Adapter calls get_viewport().set_input_as_handled(); layers and the debug overlay define no _input
decisions.reason: _input is delivered in reverse tree order and process_priority does not affect it, so any later handling node would silently starve the ring

decisions.chosen: Virtual cursor from stored cursor_off plus accumulated MouseMotion.relative, latched when a warp reads back more than WARP_READBACK_TOLERANCE_PX; cursor mode re-asserted on FOCUS_IN and PAUSED->RUNNING; Input.warp_mouse is the one call; virtual cursor lives in the Adapter, so the InputSource port stays at ten methods
decisions.reason: warp_mouse support on Linux/Wayland (RM-DECK) and in the embedded editor window is unverified; zoom and handover must not depend on it

registry_candidates.name: input_sampling_and_edges
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: input_sampling_and_edges
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed
    api: "InputAdapter._input (added as the LAST child of its parent so it runs first; _input order is reverse tree order, process_priority does not affect it) latches ordered press/release records for key, mouse-button and pad-button events, wheel presses (pressed==true WHEEL_UP/DOWN only) and pointer events into a preallocated EdgeRing de-duplicated against a held-set, and submits nothing; InputEventJoypadMotion is continuous-only (no edge record); InputAdapter._process (INPUT_ADAPTER -100) drains the ring, polls Input.get_action_raw_strength for continuous families, derives stick and trigger edges once per frame with hysteresis, and is the only place submit() is called, in the order set_move_intent, set_aim, commands; the Adapter uses _input (not _unhandled_input) and is the only caller of get_viewport().set_input_as_handled() for action-bound events"
    not: "polling just_pressed/just_released alone (a same-frame press and release cannot be ordered, probed 2026-10-29); _unhandled_input latching; recording pad-axis motion as edges; calling set_input_as_handled as a Node method (it is Viewport's); _input or set_input_as_handled in any layer, HUD or debug overlay; submit from _input, a signal handler or _physics_process; input buffering (ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS 0)"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    reason: "Ordered edges are needed by latch-until-released, fresh-press and hold-cancel rules; a focused Control would otherwise consume a press before _unhandled_input; a later node handling an event first would starve the ring; pad-axis motion reports pressed on every event; one tick of latency"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: "2026-10-29 (review: E2, E3, E4, E7)"

decisions.chosen: Read-time scalar getters (get_chest_x/y, get_hand_x/y -> int) over BodyView.pos_x/pos_y plus a frozen ControllerCatalog table keyed [sheet][row], row from loco_state; nothing stored; post_restore recomputes cap_seen only

registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: input_sampling_and_edges
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed
    api: "InputAdapter._input (added as the LAST child of its parent so it runs first; _input order is reverse tree order, process_priority does not affect it) latches ordered press/release records for key, mouse-button and pad-button events, wheel presses (pressed==true WHEEL_UP/DOWN only) and pointer events into a preallocated EdgeRing de-duplicated against a held-set, and submits nothing; InputEventJoypadMotion is continuous-only (no edge record); InputAdapter._process (INPUT_ADAPTER -100) drains the ring, polls Input.get_action_raw_strength for continuous families, derives stick and trigger edges once per frame with hysteresis, and is the only place submit() is called, in the order set_move_intent, set_aim, commands; the Adapter uses _input (not _unhandled_input) and is the only caller of get_viewport().set_input_as_handled() for action-bound events"
    not: "polling just_pressed/just_released alone (a same-frame press and release cannot be ordered, probed 2026-10-29); _unhandled_input latching; recording pad-axis motion as edges; calling set_input_as_handled as a Node method (it is Viewport's); _input or set_input_as_handled in any layer, HUD or debug overlay; submit from _input, a signal handler or _physics_process; input buffering (ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS 0)"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    reason: "Ordered edges are needed by latch-until-released, fresh-press and hold-cancel rules; a focused Control would otherwise consume a press before _unhandled_input; a later node handling an event first would starve the ring; pad-axis motion reports pressed on every event; one tick of latency"
    referenced_by:

    api: "Devices are identified by event type (RawEvent.classify: InputEventKey, InputEventMouse*, InputEventJoypad*); every InputMap binding built in code, including a user-captured one (BindingFactory.from_capture duplicates the event, sets device = BINDING_ANY_DEVICE (-1) and clears pressed/echo), uses the any-device wildcard, and keyboard bindings use physical_keycode; the only numeric use of InputEvent.device is comparing a pad event with the stored active_pad variable"
    not: "event.device == 0 or any integer literal; comparison with DEVICE_ID_* constants; a binding left at its constructor device or stored from a captured event directly (a pad binding defaults to device 0 and matches only pad 0, probed 2026-10-29 on 4.7.2)"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    reason: "4.7 changed the keyboard and mouse device numbers and pads are numbered by enumeration; bindings keep their constructor or captured device"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: "2026-10-29 (review: E8 capture path)"

registry_candidates.name: input_action_deadzone_nonzero
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: input_action_deadzone_nonzero
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed
    api: "BindingFactory registers every catalogue action with InputMap.add_action(name, ENGINE_ACTION_DEADZONE) where the constant is non-zero (engine default 0.5 or 0.2); MOVE_DEADZONE and AIM_DEADZONE are Adapter-level scalings over get_action_raw_strength, which ignores the engine deadzone; a boot lint fails when InputMap.action_get_deadzone is 0.0 for any catalogue action"
    not: "add_action(name, 0.0); reading Input.is_action_pressed for a gameplay decision on an analogue family"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    reason: "Probed on 4.7.2: with a 0.0 deadzone a centred stick (axis_value 0.0) and a trigger at rest report their action pressed in both directions (abs(0.0) >= 0.0)"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: chest_hand_point_read_time_getters
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: chest_hand_point_read_time_getters
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed
    api: "ControllerView.get_chest_x/get_chest_y/get_hand_x/get_hand_y(player_id) -> int return an absolute body-frame integer: BodyView.pos_x/pos_y(actor) plus CHEST_POINT[sheet][row] (or HAND_POINT) from the frozen ADR-0007 ControllerCatalog table injected through ControllerTuning, mirrored by facing, row from loco_state; computed on every read, O(1), allocation-free; ADR-0017 reads exactly get_chest_x/get_chest_y, get_aim_angle and get_loco_state"
    not: "a stored chest_sim/hand_sim written in controller.step (one tick stale against the foot origin); a Vector2i on the per-tick Emitter path; a second source of the offsets in the presentation sidecar"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    reason: "controller.step runs before body.integrate, ADR-0017 reads the apex after it; a read-time getter cannot lag, and the apex and occlusion origin agree by construction (ADR-0018)"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: aim_quantisation_and_mapping
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: aim_quantisation_and_mapping
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed
    api: "Mouse aim is computed once per frame as RenderLayout.mouse_to_world_aim(cursor_px, f_q) minus the fixed aim origin (BodyView.pos_x/pos_y(actor) + AIM_ORIGIN_Y), aim_q = posmod(roundi(theta * AIM_UNITS / TAU), AIM_UNITS) (round first, then posmod), sent as an int; the Adapter forms no picture-origin subtraction itself; the OS cursor is warped with Input.warp_mouse (window pixels) on a zoom edge using the stored cursor_off and on a source handover, with a virtual-cursor fallback (accumulated InputEventMouseMotion.relative) when the warp is a no-op"
    not: "mouse_to_world_view or pose_q in the aim path; a second picture-origin subtraction; a float reaching submit(); wrapping before rounding; Viewport.warp_mouse"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    reason: "pose_q contains the look-ahead, which is a function of aim; the open-loop f_q form cannot feed back"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: "2026-10-29 (review: scalar position, Input.warp_mouse, virtual cursor)"

registry_candidates.name: intent_resync_rule
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: intent_resync_rule
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed
    api: "The Adapter keeps last_acked per intent kind and sets it UNKNOWN (one change-filter bypass, rate-limited to one per AIM_SEND_INTERVAL ticks) on five labelled triggers: not-ok intent result (STALE), kernel leaves PAUSED, LOADING to RUNNING (load_seq change), focus or pad return, body_of_actor change; the first RUNNING frame after any non-RUNNING frame resyncs at -100 so it lands in P2 of the first tick; the Adapter is silent while the kernel is not RUNNING; equivalence-harness fixtures that include controller.state snapshot from a rest intent or replay the resync submission"
    not: "per-tick held-state commands; resync from a kernel hook; a persisted last_acked; submitting while PAUSED"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    reason: "The simulation's intent must equal the player's hands within one tick of RUNNING at a fraction of the traffic"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: "2026-10-29 (review: harness input model, CT-49)"

registry_candidates.name: input_context_machine
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: input_context_machine
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed
    api: "Adapter-local InputContextMachine holds exactly one of GAMEPLAY, CHART_TABLE, INSPECT_CARD, CHAT (CHAT is VS-B: enum value and matrix column reserved, transitions not implemented at MVP); the context x action matrix is data (assets/data/input/context_matrix.json, completeness check skips reserved columns) and the return table is code with one test per row; STAGGERED, DOWNED, DEAD and IN_POD force GAMEPLAY; CursorPolicy maps GAMEPLAY and INSPECT_CARD to MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED_HIDDEN and CHART_TABLE and CHAT to MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE, applied on change and re-asserted on FOCUS_IN and PAUSED->RUNNING; the Adapter holds no ControlHandle and the Chart Table layer's PauseGate issues request_pause"
    not: "a context persisted in a snapshot; a custom cursor image in gameplay; the Adapter calling the control plane"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    reason: "Contexts are presentation; the simulation only sees the zero intent and cancel the Adapter submits on entry"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    added: 2026-10-29
    revised: "2026-10-29 (review: VS-B reservation, cursor re-assert)"

registry_candidates.name: device_id_literal_compare
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: device_id_literal_compare
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed

registry_candidates.name: input_read_outside_adapter_files
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: input_read_outside_adapter_files
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed
    description: "Input.*, InputMap, InputEvent and subclasses, _input, _unhandled_input, _unhandled_key_input and _shortcut_input appear only in the files listed in tools/lint/config/allowlists/input_surface.json (input_adapter.gd, engine_input_source.gd, binding_factory.gd, raw_event.gd, dev_actions.gd); set_input_as_handled only in input_adapter.gd; get_mouse_position, warp_mouse, joy_connection_changed, focus_exited and the two focus notification constants only in engine_input_source.gd; the pipeline root, HUD, Chart Table layer, debug overlay, Instruments and Presenter read no device and define no _input (lint CTL-07)."
    why: "One door to the devices makes input replayable and keeps the Chart Table layer, pipeline root and HUD from forking their own input handling or starving the Adapter's ring."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    referenced_by:

registry_candidates.name: adapter_writes_block_or_reads_perception
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: adapter_writes_block_or_reads_perception
    status: active           # ADR-0019 is Proposed
    description: "The Input Adapter and the Avatar Presenter write no block and hold no ModuleFacet or WriteScope (lint CTL-01); no file under src/sim/controller/ or src/presentation/controller/ reads Attention, Sanity or PERCEPTION_OUT (get_view(&\"attention.state\"), AttentionView/SanityView, perceived(, PerceptionRef, true_value), the single allowed exception being the injected Attention mutator's push_stimulus in controller_noise.gd; the Controller Sim's Suit read-view requests are locomotion_cap and stowed_heavy only (lint CTL-08); mass_g, instance_mass_g, weight_class and salvage_yield never appear in the Controller (lint CTL-03)."
    why: "Input mapping, deadzones and aim source are HR-6 anchors that must be structurally unable to lie; carry speed is independent of mass; controller.noise must still be able to push its stimulus."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: controller_writes_body_position
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:

    why: "PC-14 position ownership; a same-tick Controller write after a pod hop must not displace the arrival cell (TR-shipbody-048)."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0019-player-controller-split-and-input-contexts.md
    referenced_by:
